html:
A British attack on Benin City in February 1897, sent after the kingdom's men had killed a British party that tried to visit the Oba during a sacred festival.

About 1,200 British troops took the city, burned much of it and looted thousands of brass plaques, heads and ivory carvings, the Benin Bronzes, which were sold to museums across Europe and the United States. The Oba, Ovonramwen, was exiled to Calabar, and the kingdom was added to the British protectorate. Since the 2010s several museums and countries have returned objects to Nigeria. See also the Walls of Benin.
